title: Custom Docker builds
idea: A custom build changes what `docker build` does: which Dockerfile it reads, which stage it stops at, and which values it receives.
points: `-f api.Dockerfile` reads another file; the context is still the folder you name.
`ARG` declares a build-time value; `--build-arg NAME=value` sets it for one build.
`--target dev` builds a multi-stage Dockerfile only up to the stage named `dev`.
An `ARG` is not set in the running container; copy it with `ENV`.

parts.label: Command
parts.note: Reads a Dockerfile and builds an image from it.

parts.label: Dockerfile
parts.note: Names the file to read. Without `-f`, Docker reads `Dockerfile` in the context.

parts.label: Build argument
parts.note: Gives the `ARG` named `APP_VERSION` a value for this build only.

parts.label: Target stage
parts.note: Builds up to the stage named `prod`. Stages after it are not built.

parts.label: Image name
parts.note: The name and tag for the new image.

parts.label: Context
parts.note: The build context: the folder Docker sends to the builder.

code.title: Stages and ARG
code.caption: One file, two buildable stages. `dev` and `prod` both start from `base`.

walk.text: An `ARG` above the first `FROM` sets the Node version. `--build-arg NODE_VERSION=…` can change it.
Shared setup lives in `base`: the working folder and the package files.
`dev` builds on `base` and installs every dependency. Build it with `--target dev`.
`prod` declares `APP_VERSION` with a default. `--build-arg APP_VERSION=…` overrides it.
`ENV` keeps the value in the image, so the app can read `process.env.APP_VERSION`.
`prod` installs production dependencies only, then copies the source.

code.title: The same build in Compose
code.caption: Compose's long `build` form. Run `docker compose build` or `docker compose up --build`.

walk.text: `context` is the build folder. A relative `dockerfile` path is resolved from `context`.
`args` sets `ARG` values for this build, like `--build-arg`.

pitfalls: Never pass secrets with `--build-arg`; they can appear in `docker history`. Use `--secret`.
An `ARG` above the first `FROM` is not visible in stages; redeclare it inside.
In Compose, a relative `dockerfile:` path starts from `context`, not from `compose.yaml`.

quiz.q: You run `docker build --target dev .` on this Dockerfile. Which stages run?
quiz.code:
FROM node:20-alpine AS base
FROM base AS dev
FROM base AS prod
quiz.why: `--target dev` stops at `dev`. That stage builds on `base`, so both run, and `prod` is not built.

takeaway: Use `ARG` and `--build-arg` for values, `--target` for stages, `-f` for files.
